profile.campus: Vantaa, Finland (Equinix HE4, part of Equinix's Helsinki-region cluster despite the registry's "Helsinki" naming)
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's HE4 facility at Myllynkivenkuja 4B, though despite carrying "Helsinki" in this registry's facility name, Equinix's own dedicated page places HE4 in the neighboring city of Vantaa, part of the same greater Helsinki metropolitan area as sibling facilities HE3, HE5, HE6, and HE7, all of which Equinix markets collectively under its Helsinki region heading. Equinix's page describes HE4 as a two-story building with 2,218 square meters, about 23,874 square feet, of colocation space, the largest of the Helsinki-region cluster's individually confirmed figures, with N+1 power and cooling redundancy including free-cooling capability, generator autonomy of 30 hours or more at full load, and a minimum cabinet density of 10kVA, plus a 99.9999%-plus global uptime guarantee; it does not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts. Equinix entered the European colocation market through its 2007 acquisition of IXEurope and expanded further through its 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about $3.8 billion, though Equinix's current HE4 page does not attribute the building to either predecessor company by name. Equinix, founded in Silicon Valley in 1998, converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX.

As an EU-based facility, this data center falls under the European Union's Energy Efficiency Directive reporting requirements, which since 2024 have required data centers above a minimum capacity threshold to report power usage effectiveness, water usage, and other sustainability metrics to a European Commission database, part of a broader EU push for standardized data center energy transparency that does not have a direct equivalent in most of the US markets covered elsewhere in this registry.

Finland has positioned itself as a Nordic data center hub in part due to its naturally cool climate, which reduces cooling energy costs, and its access to renewable hydro and wind power from the broader Nordic electricity grid; several other major operators beyond Equinix, including Google and Microsoft, have also built large-scale data centers in Finland citing similar climate and clean-power advantages.
